eywa.title: Eywa
eywa.info: Not a goddess above the world — the sum of all its life. Roots, fungal threads, and tsaheylu bonds form a planet-scale network. Grace Augustine: more connections than synapses in a human brain. Touch a node; watch the signal ripple outward.
eywa.idle: Touch a node to wake the web
eywa.hint: Each touch seeds a ripple. At full depth the web holds more links than a human connectome — the question of Part III is whether that scale can become a mind.

tsaheylu.title: Tsaheylu
tsaheylu.info: The bond. Two queues of pinkish neural tendrils interlace and open a two-way channel — motor command, sensation, and emotion in real time. Canon calls it a biological ethernet cable; the mount becomes an extension of the rider.
tsaheylu.hint: Drag the queues until the tendrils lace. Particles stream both ways once the bond locks — command out, feeling in.

unobtanium.title: Unobtanium
unobtanium.info: Pandora's room-temperature superconductor. Ore cores pin into the Flux Vortex and hold the floating mountains aloft. Drag the chunk over the magnet track; flux threads sew it in place. The amber core is the rare warm accent — heat that never quenches the superconductivity.
unobtanium.hint: Room temperature is already met. Slide the ore onto the track and the flux pins catch — not balancing, locked. The amber heart keeps glowing.

prolemuris.title: Prolemuris
prolemuris.info: An arboreal Pandoran primate with partly fused upper forelimbs — the living bridge from the six-limbed body plan shared by Pandoran animals to the four-limbed plan of the Na'vi. Canopy life favored dexterity over a spare pair of arms.
prolemuris.hint: Drag evolution from six free limbs toward a fused forearm. Prolemuris sits in the middle — evidence the Na'vi came from the same hexapod stock.
